# The rebuild kit

How to rebuild Faro from this folder and `llms.txt` alone, one stage at a time, and prove each stage works. Each stage has entry criteria (what must be true before it starts), what to build, and exit criteria (what proves it is done). A stage with a **drill** is scored by a harness against the conformance data; an **outline** stage has its criteria written down but nothing to score it yet.

## The stages

| Stage | Builds | Today |
|---|---|---|
| [1. The core rules](stage-1-core-rules.md) | Weeks and plans, a goal’s status, the projection, what a check-in must say, flags and needs attention, and the scorecard: pure functions over the records, with no screens and no database. | Drill ready: the harness scores it |
| [2. The core data and the change engine](stage-2-core-data.md) | Every core record stored, the change log with undo, and the change engine that takes many changes at once and checks them with the stage 1 rules. | Drill ready: the harness scores it |
| [3. The core screens and journeys](stage-3-core-screens.md) | Each core screen with its route, named parts and one main action, so a person can do every core journey. | Drill ready: the harness scores it |
| [4. Module: Feedback](stage-4-module-feedback.md) | Feedback, as a feature a workspace can switch off. Anyone can send feedback about Faro (a mood and a few words) or mark up the screen they are on (a still picture with marks and a line, from Send feedback or Ctrl+Shift+M), and everything sent goes to the builders' inbox, the page Feedback, which the people who build Faro work through from New to In hand to Closed, and which an AI tool can review. Off, Feedback leaves the menu, Send feedback and Mark up this screen go, Ctrl+Shift+M does nothing, /feedback says it is switched off and who can switch it on, and the inbox's tools and send_feedback refuse. What was sent stays in the builders' inbox. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [5. Module: Goal map](stage-5-module-goal-map.md) | The Goal map, as a feature a workspace can switch off: one of Goals' layouts, drawing every goal on a canvas, north stars at the top, solid lines for feeds into and dotted for also helps, with the critical path bold and each goal's roll-up of what feeds it. It owns no records. Off, Goals offers List, Table, Board and History, and a link or saved view that asked for the Map (view=map) opens the List and says once “The Goal map is off here, so this is the List.” | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [6. Module: Metric library](stage-6-module-metrics.md) | The metric library, and the worked example of a module with records of its own. A metric (name, meaning and calculation, unit, decimals, which way is better, source and its owner, refresh, owner, caveats) is defined once per workspace, and a goal links to one metric for a slice (a team, or the whole company), the goal’s own target being the target in it. Anyone adds a metric; its owner or an admin changes or removes it; the goal’s owner or an admin links and unlinks. Every change is logged, removing and unlinking keep the row and come back with Undo or Recently removed, and the AI tools do the same under the same rules. Its two records are its own, not the core’s: the module declares each (what one row is, its table, where a save and the workspace file it, whether it can be removed) with its rows each way, what a new cycle carries over (every metric not removed; the links in force to the cycle’s live goals) and how a removed metric comes back, and the core’s store, removal, restore, cycle and export keep them without knowing what they are. Its rules sit in its own folder, as pure as the core’s. Its own place, /metrics: the library (find by name, unit, owner or meaning; filter by unit, the team or the whole company a goal measures it for, owner, direction, unused, or something to sort out; sort A to Z, by most goals or by the latest change; 50 a page), a page per metric with its meaning, every goal measured by it side by side (status, slice, now, target, against plan) and what it still needs, an item in the menu after People, and the metric on a goal’s page and on a person’s and a team’s. “Measured by” in the goal forms: find a metric by typing (or add one there); choosing it on a new goal fills in its unit, decimals and direction; Goals filters by the metric. Defining one well: three things to be usable, the rest said later and named in words (“Fully defined” or “Still to say: …”, never a score), and three questions answered once before saving (a close name, a unit spelt another way, a percentage that doesn’t say out of what), with each Must fix and Check under its field. For, and which part: a link is for a team or the whole company and optionally one part of that number (“tier-1 services”), the parts in use offered under the field; the goal takes the metric’s unit and direction, its target stays its own; another goal on the same number, or a part spelt like one in use, is asked about once; and a goal with check-ins says why it is measured differently, in its History. Looking after one: what it still needs, a confirm before changing a unit or direction goals use, and on Workspace → About how many metrics have no owner. Measurement status: each metric says whether it is measured today (Measured, Partly or Gap, a shape and a word, with what is missing); a gap or a part is listed under To sort out, and a goal measured by a gap is held to no number (the core’s rule over the goal’s own field, which the library fills in when it links the goal and when the metric is measured). | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [7. Module: Reviews](stage-7-module-reviews.md) | Reviews, as a feature a workspace can switch off. A review walks a set of goals together on a cadence (every 1, 2 or 4 weeks, on a weekday): its agenda puts the goals that need attention first, worst and stalest, and the walk opens each goal's page in turn, where someone in the review marks it reviewed, adds a note, asks the owner a question, agrees a next step with who and by when, or accepts the risk on a goal behind; a goal off track or at risk leaves the walk with a decision. What was said stays on each goal: questions and next steps are asks, open on the owner's Home until answered or done; a held session leads its page with what was said, and prints. Off, Reviews has no menu row or phone tab, no page (its addresses say it is switched off and who can switch it on), no Next review on Home, no Last time we talked or walk on a goal, no review tools for an assistant and no review asked for on Workspace; asks and next steps stay as they are, History keeps what was said, and switching it back on brings every review back as it was. An admin switches it off on Workspace, Features, after a read-back that counts what stays. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [8. Module: Spreadsheets](stage-8-module-spreadsheets.md) | Download every goal, plan number, check-in, person and ask as one Excel workbook or a zip of CSV files in the one spreadsheet format, with a first sheet, Start here, made from the field table (what a new row needs in each column, its format, an example, what an empty cell does); a template with only the columns a person fills in and example rows; and load a workbook, a zip or one CSV back: every row goes through the change engine (stage 2), is shown before it is saved, and saves all at once or not at all. Every problem the engine finds is data with a kind and a level (core rule: kinds, levels and near misses): Must fix blocks saving, a Check is a question answered once for every row with it, and a name or word one letter out is asked about, never guessed. Before anything is saved, a preview says which sheets and columns were read and which were not (a column nothing reads is named, never dropped), counts by sheet, then what must be fixed, then the questions, then every change on request with before and after and every default used; the rows to fix download with a Problem column, or are left out with the rows that depend on them while the rest saves. Export is one sheet with one button, Export .xlsx (the other formats behind Other formats), the file’s name shown before it saves and said after; on Data, Export saves the table as shown and Import sits beside it. Every file is named workspace, what, scope (all, the view’s name, or as-shown) and date; the template is faro-template.xlsx. Help’s table of every column. Saving ends on Imported (what was saved from which file, and Undo); every import, bulk edit and change through MCP is one line in Past imports and one entry in Activity (its rows folded under it), and can be undone as a whole by whoever made it or an admin, saying first which rows changed since and stay, and why (core rule: undoing an import). A large file (more than 500 rows) is checked off the page’s thread: after 400 ms, Reading {file} says how far the check has got and what it has found so far, with Stop (“Stopped. Nothing was saved.”); the changes and a question’s rows are drawn 50 at a time; a file that would change more than 5,000 rows is checked, not saved, and offered as {k} files of 5,000 rows, each goal with its plan and check-ins and a goal before the goals that feed into it (core rule: the change engine, Speed). Saving tens of thousands of rows is the platform’s server-side job (internal requirement R11, R-L1 to R-L6); the browser’s preview is advice. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [9. Module: Fields](stage-9-module-tags.md) | Fields, as a feature a workspace can switch off: a workspace defines up to six of its own fields on goals (a stage, a programme), each a list of 1 to 20 values or free text; a goal has at most one value per field. No rule reads a field: it is for finding and sorting. Its two records are its own (a field, and a goal's value for one), kept, saved and carried by the core without it knowing what they are; a field is never deleted, only retired and brought back with its values. Workspace → Fields (/workspace/fields) lists the fields in order with their kind and how many goals have a value; admins add one (its one primary action), rename it, change a list's values, move it up or down, retire it and bring it back, and everyone else reads them. A goal's page has a Fields block in About, after its facts: one line per live field, “Stage · Build” or “Stage · Not set”, which the goal's owner or an admin changes in place (a select for a list, up to 80 characters of free text), with no reason asked; History says “Stage: Discover → Build”, and “Stage added”, “Stage retired”. Goals' Filters sheet has a row per live list field (its values and “Not set”, any of them ticked), the filter line says “Stage is Build” with Remove, and the address carries it as /goals?f.<field id>=Build so a link and a saved view keep it; free text is not a filter. Data's Goals table and every export's Goals sheet have a column per live field, headed with its name; loaded back, a field's cell changes the goal's value under the same rules as its page, an export loaded straight back changes nothing, and a value a list doesn't hold is asked once per value (“Stage says “Operate” on 4 rows. Add “Operate” to Stage, or leave these cells empty?”), which only an admin may add. An assistant lists the fields (list_fields), sets a goal's values by field name with dry_run (set_goal_fields), finds goals by them (find_goals' fields) and, as an admin, defines them (save_field), under the same rules. Off, there is no Fields block, no Fields in Workspace's menu, no field filter on Goals and no field column on Data or in an export (a file's are columns nothing reads, named once), /workspace/fields says Fields is switched off and who can switch it on, and the three tools and find_goals' fields refuse; every field and value stays, and comes back when it is switched on. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [10. Module: Watching](stage-10-module-watching.md) | Watching, as a feature a workspace can switch off. Anyone can watch a goal, a goal and everything feeding it, or every goal at a level; the goals a person's watches cover are on their Home under “Goals you watch” (what needs attention first) and under the Watching tab of Goals, a goal's page has Watch (or Watching) for anyone but its owner, and an AI tool lists, adds and stops watches. Off, there is no Watching tab, no “Goals you watch”, no Watch button and no watching tool; /watching says it is switched off and who can switch it on; someone who owns no goal is led to every goal that needs attention. Every watch is kept, and switching it back on restores each person's. An admin switches it off on Workspace, Features, after a read-back that counts what stays. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |
| [11. Module: Wrap-up](stage-11-module-wrap-up.md) | The Wrap-up, as a feature a workspace can switch off: in the last two weeks of the year (and four weeks after) each owner says how each goal landed, one thing learned, and whether it carries on or stops, from Home's wrap-up lead, a goal's “Wrap up this goal” and the page Wrap up. Results, carrying on and starting the next year are the core's and never switch off. Off, nobody is asked how a goal landed: no wrap-up lead on Home, no “See the wrap-up”, no “Wrap up this goal”, /retro says it is switched off, and get_wrap_up and wrap_up_goal refuse; wrap-ups already written stay in History, and an admin still starts the next year from Cycles. | Outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand; no drill yet |

**What the kit fully supports today:** stages 1, 2, 3. Stage 1 has everything a rebuild needs in this folder: the records it reads, the rules in plain words with worked examples, the conformance data for every goal in every week of the demo workspace (43373 rows in five files, one of them every check-in judged again by what a check-in must say), and a harness that runs a rebuild and scores it. Only Numbers and names is shown by worked examples alone, with no conformance rows. Stages 2 and 3 have a drill for part of what they build: stage 2’s scores the change engine (what it raises, and what each change set would save, item by item), stage 3’s the screens’ words that are rules (the menu and a page’s name, New goal’s read-back, Find, Home’s lead). The rest of each, the store, undo and the screens themselves, is still checked by hand; their pages say which.

**Copying the code instead of rebuilding it?** The stage for that is [swap the outside parts](adapters.md): write an adapter for each part of the outside world your platform provides (the database, sign-in, files, where numbers come from), until its contract test passes. It sits beside the numbered stages, not after them: a team that copies Faro does it first and may need none of the others. Its goals store is the demo-scale port: before building on it for the whole company, read [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md), the query and command ports that replace it. To prove a rebuild holds at company size, [accepting scale](scale.md) has a workspace of that size to load and the week’s turn’s budget. And before copying anything, read [don’t copy this](dont-copy.md): what is right for a demo and wrong for the internal app.

**What is an outline:** every stage after 3. Their pages say what to build and what proves it, so a rebuild can start, but the proof is by hand, and each lists the gaps where the kit doesn’t yet hold what a rebuild needs. Each grows a drill as the kit grows (backlog item 8k: every item adds its module’s stage and runs its drill).

## What Faro doesn’t build

Some things the internal app must do, Faro leaves to the platform it is rebuilt on, so no stage builds them from Faro’s code. They are written as requirements, each with acceptance checks and the stage it lands nearest to: [the requirements for the internal app](../requirements/internal/README.md).

- [R1. Sign-in and access](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md): who can see and change what, workspace membership, AI and builder tokens, who may read a sent markup
- [R2. Company single sign-on](../requirements/internal/r2-single-sign-on.md): signing in through the company’s identity provider, and leavers losing access the day they leave
- [R3. Time zones](../requirements/internal/r3-time-zones.md): real moments stored, shown in the viewer’s zone, a home zone per workspace, reviews with a time and zone
- [R4. Scale and safety](../requirements/internal/r4-scale-and-safety.md): 15,000 people: summary rows on the server, paging, page-load budgets, backups and restore, rehearsed migrations, the master key
- [R5. Notifications and the weekly habit](../requirements/internal/r5-notifications-and-habits.md): asks, one reminder and a weekly digest in set words, check-in from a notification, never shame, streaks that forgive, the habit measure, a role per workspace
- [R6a. The organisation](../requirements/internal/r6a-organisation.md): teams in a tree, people with managers, levels set per workspace, and every list and count scoped to a part of the company
- [R6b. Delegates](../requirements/internal/r6b-delegates.md): someone named to check in and answer asks for an owner while they are away, recorded as acting for them
- [R6c. The planning round](../requirements/internal/r6c-planning-round.md): next cycle’s goals drafted, proposed and agreed before they go live, and counted nowhere until then
- [R7. Data retention, privacy and erasure](../requirements/internal/r7-retention-and-privacy.md): what is personal, how long each record is kept, leavers, seeing everything held about you, erasure
- [R8. Audit](../requirements/internal/r8-audit.md): a record of who did what that no one can change, with exports and token use, kept 7 years
- [R9. Observability and service levels](../requirements/internal/r9-observability.md): the signals sent to the company’s tools, the service levels promised, and what pages the on-call person
- [R10. Accessibility](../requirements/internal/r10-accessibility.md): WCAG 2.2 AA on every screen: shape and word, the keyboard, screen readers, zoom and reflow
- [R11. Large imports, a server-side job](../requirements/internal/r11-large-imports.md): an import of tens of thousands of rows as a job on the server: the rules run there, one state at the end, Undo kept per import (R-L1 to R-L6)
- [R12. Number sources](../requirements/internal/r12-number-sources.md): connectors for where metrics’ numbers are kept: credentials on the server, a reference per metric and slice, readings on a schedule with revisions, failures to the source’s owner (R12.1 to R12.8)

## The drill: a fresh session rebuilds a stage from the kit alone

The drill is the test of the kit, not of the rebuild: whatever the session had to guess shows where the kit is short, and goes back into it.

### What the session gets

A scratch folder holding a copy of `spec/` and `llms.txt`, and nothing else from Faro. Node 18 or later is enough to run the harness (it uses no packages). The spec links to files in Faro’s repository (`src/…`, `docs/…`, `evals/…`): they are not in the kit. Don’t look for them; when a link is the only place something is said, write it down as a gap.

### Where to write

```
<scratch folder>/
  llms.txt          read only
  spec/             read only: the kit, unchanged
  rebuild/          everything you write goes here
    drill.json      { "stage": 1, "run": "node main.mjs" }   how the harness runs your rebuild (stage 1, 2 or 3)
    main.mjs        (or any language: "run" is any command that works in this folder)
    GAPS.md         what you had to guess, and where the kit should have said it
    drill-out/      written by the harness on every run; leave it out of your code
```

### How to score it

From the scratch folder:

```
node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild
node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild --files status          one file while you work (stage 1: status, flags, projection, scorecard, checkin;
                                                            stage 2: changes, import; stage 3: navigation, readback, find, home)
node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild --diffs 30              more of the first differences
```

From Faro’s own repository the same harness is `npm run drill -- <rebuild folder>`. It runs `drill.json`’s command, scores the files its stage writes, file by file and column by column, prints the first differences (with the week, the goal and the column), and exits 0 only at 100%.

### The rules of the drill

1. Read only `spec/` and `llms.txt`. Nothing from Faro’s repository, its live app or anywhere else.
2. Don’t change `spec/`. Write only under `rebuild/`.
3. The rebuild computes every row from the workspace it is given (the first argument). It never reads the expected CSV files in `spec/conformance/`; the harness hands it a copy of `workspace.json` in a folder of its own.
4. Keep `rebuild/GAPS.md` as you go: each thing you had to guess, what you guessed, whether the score proved it right, and which spec page should have said it. A gap the conformance data settled still counts: the words should have said it.
5. Finish with the harness’s last output and `GAPS.md`.

## Keeping it true

- These pages are made by `npm run spec` (`src/spec/rebuild.ts`); never edit them by hand.
- A module’s stage comes from its `module.json` (`rebuild`: status, what it builds, entry, exit and gaps). CI fails when a module in `src/modules` has no stage here (`scripts/check-rebuild.mjs`).
- The harness is `scripts/drill.mjs`, copied here as `drill.mjs`. CI runs it on Faro’s own rules (`scripts/drill-faro`), which must score 100% on every stage’s files.
